analysis.investment_thesis: Chalet operates premium business hotels in high-barrier micro-markets (Mumbai, Hyderabad, Bengaluru), giving it some location-based pricing power amid India's under-supplied upper-upscale segment. However, ROIC below 12%, a net profit collapse from ₹278 Cr to ₹142 Cr in FY25 despite 21% revenue growth, and ₹969 Cr capex that turned FCF negative make this a 'show me' story at a 28x P/E.
key_strengths: Operating margin of 35.5% and EBITDA CAGR of 14% over 9 years reflect real pricing power in premium hotel micro-markets
OCF grew from ₹60 Cr (FY21) to ₹950 Cr (FY25), demonstrating genuine post-COVID operational recovery
Near-complete equity raise (equity base doubled to ₹3,415 Cr) significantly de-risked the balance sheet; net debt now ~₹2,495 Cr vs EBITDA ₹765 Cr (3.3x)
key_risks: ROIC (ROCE 11.1%) sits below Munger's 12% minimum threshold — the business does not yet earn its cost of capital
Massive capex cycle (₹969 Cr in FY25, rising CWIP) locks capital into illiquid hotel assets with long gestation; FCF turned negative at -₹14 Cr
Net profit volatility is extreme — losses in 4 of 9 years; FY25 profit halved despite revenue growth, likely due to depreciation on new assets and softer RevPAR growth
red_flags: FY25 net profit ₹142 Cr on revenues of ₹1,718 Cr implies 8.3% net margin — dangerously thin for a 28x P/E valuation
Business mixes hotel operations with real estate development, creating accounting opacity and capital misallocation risk — complexity Munger despises
ROE of just 5.77% means shareholders are earning well below the risk-free rate on book value
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Chalet is a genuinely improving hospitality business riding India's structural travel and corporate accommodation tailwind, but it remains hostage to its asset-heavy model and real estate development overlay. The FY25 profit decline from ₹278 Cr to ₹142 Cr while revenues grew 21% is a warning sign — the capex-driven depreciation load is eroding earnings quality even as cash generation improves. Finance cost reduction (CAGR -3.3%) and OCF of ₹950 Cr are positives, but a large part of that cash is immediately being re-deployed into aggressive expansion (₹1,355 Cr investing outflow in FY25).

At 28x P/E and 16.8x EV/EBITDA for a sub-12% ROCE business, the market is pricing in a perfect execution of a heavy capex cycle over 3–5 years. I prefer to wait until new assets stabilize and ROIC crosses 15% sustainably. The K Raheja promoter group (67.3% holding) has long hotel experience, but the conglomerate nature of the parent adds governance complexity. Not a business I would put serious capital into at this price.
